title: Completion-at-point exit function acceptance

environment.system_features: ACL GMP GNUTLS LIBSELINUX LIBXML2 MODULES NATIVE_COMP NOTIFY INOTIFY PDUMPER SECCOMP SQLITE3 THREADS TREE_SITTER ZLIB

mechanism: CAPF metadata can include a provider-owned `:exit-function'; faithful acceptance must run that function, not merely produce the same buffer text.
hypothesis: Accepting a sole candidate through `completion-at-point' should insert the candidate and call `:exit-function' with the accepted string and status, while a raw text replacement can produce identical text without that side effect.
minimal_fixture: Two temporary buffers starting with `fo': one uses a synthetic CAPF for `foobar', the other deletes and inserts the same final text directly.
predicted_behavior: The CAPF path and raw insertion path converge on the same text, but only the CAPF path records the provider exit event.
observed_behavior: capf-return=t capf-text="foobar" capf-events=(("foobar" finished)) raw-text="foobar" raw-events=nil

independent_checks.name: CAPF acceptance produced the expected text
CAPF acceptance ran provider exit function
raw replacement produced the same final text
raw replacement skipped provider exit function

counterexample: A ghost-text or model-completion accept path can appear text-correct while skipping provider side effects such as imports, snippets, caches, or backend state transitions.
derived_gym_requirement: Completion acceptance evidence must record whether a provider exit function existed, whether it ran, which candidate/status it saw, and whether the edit path was CAPF, preview, or a separate model overlay.
